problem: Plante plates are described as 'thin'. In standard construction the Plante plate is a thick, solid cast lead plate, formed by cycling; its thickness and pure lead are exactly why it lasts long but stores little energy per kilogram. Calling it thin contradicts the textbooks and the reason given for its low energy density.
fix: Section 2: 'They are thick and hold less energy per kilogram, but they last long, so they suit standby work.' Quiz Q4: 'giving a thick, durable plate of lower capacity per kilogram.'

problem: The per-cell figure and the whole-battery figure do not match: 6 × 2.3 V = 13.8 V, not 14.1 V. A student who multiplies will get a different number from the one printed.
fix: 'Above about 2.3 to 2.4 V per cell (roughly 13.8 to 14.4 V for the whole battery)'. Use the same pair in the exam traps.

problem: 'Series connection also lets the pack deliver the very high cranking current' is misleading. Series connection raises voltage, not current capability; the hundreds of amperes come from the large plate area and the few milliohms of internal resistance.
fix: 'The series connection gives the 12.6 V the starter needs; the large plate area and the few milliohms of internal resistance let the pack push out hundreds of amperes, with the terminal voltage sagging by a volt or two.'
